scenario: [RTIM.3.2.6]'s second half: after one clock move, "an expression that reads the time reads the new instant". The timeline is `RTIM.3.2.6_one_move_does_everything_due`'s: at 0 the harness asserts Go, a Short (ttl 2 s) and a Long (ttl 4 s), and pumps, so `wait` arms `after 3_s`. Then one `advance` of 5 s and one pump. The timer's follow-up runs in that pump, and its body reads the clock: `emit Fired t: monotonic_ns()` ([LTIM.2.2.2]), read inside the `after` body so that it is the follow-up's read and not the arming firing's. A runtime that does the timer at the new instant reads 5 s, so `read_new` fires and emits a ReadNew; one that visits the instant the move skipped, running the timer at its own deadline, reads 3 s, so `read_due` fires instead and no ReadNew is emitted. Live after the second pump: Go, Fired and ReadNew, so 3; the TTL facts have expired and the compiler's timer and capture facts are discharged ([LTAC.3.1]). `read_due` is in `dead_rules_expected`, so a 3 s read also fails by name ([RCTS.1.2.17]). Each check rule has one positive pattern and compares a slot with a literal, so neither makes a time-dependent read ([LEXP.9.6.1]). PATH PINNED: the deadline drain at the pump after a clock move, and the clock a firing in that drain reads: libds's timer dispatch and `FN_MONOTONIC_NS`, and the Mercury runtime's one deadline structure (`ds.engine`) and its clock token. That the TTL deadlines are done at the new instant is pinned by `RTIM.3.2.6_due_deadlines_carry_the_new_instant`.
rules_ds:
schema Go scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema Short scope ttl 2_s:
    v: Int

schema Long scope ttl 4_s:
    v: Int

schema Fired scope ttl 1_h:
    t: Duration

schema ReadNew scope ttl 1_h:
    v: Int

rule wait:
    Go
->
    after 3_s:
        emit Fired t: monotonic_ns()

rule read_new:
    Fired f where f.t == 5_s
->
    emit ReadNew v: 1

rule read_due:
    Fired f where f.t == 3_s
->
    log info "the timer read its own deadline"
